title: Formalisme algébrique des correspondances et algèbres de Poincaré-Hodge (cf conjectures standard) : notes manuscrites (s.d.), tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), lettres (1966-1967).

deep.reconstruction:
Letter to John Coates dated 6 January 1966. It follows up Grothendieck's talk on the standard conjectures (the previous page is the end of an earlier letter to him). Setting: X is smooth projective of dimension n, H is a Weil cohomology, twists are ignored, and L_X is cup product with a hyperplane class. In the notation of this period, C_χ(X) appears to be the Lefschetz-type standard conjecture (later B(X) / A(X,L)): the hard Lefschetz isomorphism v = L^{n-i}: H^i → H^{2n-i} has an inverse induced by an algebraic correspondence. D_χ(X) is 'homological = numerical equivalence'.

Proposition. C_χ(X) is equivalent to each of the following.
(a) D_χ(X) holds, and for every i<n there exists some algebraic isomorphism H^{2n-i} → H^i. Only its effect in that one degree is constrained.
(b) Every algebraic endomorphism of H^i has a characteristic polynomial with rational coefficients, and for every i<n some algebraic isomorphism H^{2n-i} → H^i exists.

Proof.
- C ⇒ (a) is clear.
- (a) ⇒ (b): D implies rationality of characteristic polynomials of algebraic endomorphisms, as sketched in the talk.
- (b) ⇒ C: let u: H^{2n-i} → H^i be the given algebraic isomorphism, v = L^{n-i}, and w = uv, an algebraic automorphism of H^i.
- By Cayley–Hamilton, w^b − σ_1 w^{b-1} + ... + (−1)^b σ_b = 0 with σ_b = det w ≠ 0. Hence w^{-1} is a polynomial in w with coefficients ±σ_j/σ_b, which are rational by hypothesis.
- So w^{-1} is induced by a Q-linear combination of powers of the correspondence for w, together with the diagonal for the w^0 term. Then v^{-1} = w^{-1}u is algebraic (continued on the next page).

Purposes:
- Condition (b) does not mention L, so C_χ(X) is independent of the polarization.
- It isolates the real content of the Lefschetz conjecture: H^i should be 'motivically' isomorphic to its dual H^{2n-i}.
- The next page adds: in characteristic 0 the rationality condition is automatic, so C ⇔ existence of algebraic isomorphisms H^{2n-i} → H^i.
- Corollary on the next page: inverses of algebraic isomorphisms between cohomologies of varieties satisfying C are algebraic.
- It then gestures at semisimplicity of the algebra of correspondences under C plus the Hodge index condition.
errors: Minor imprecision: the 'identity' term (w^0) in the Cayley–Hamilton expression must be realised algebraically. The diagonal does this, since only the action on H^i matters, which is exactly the caveat Grothendieck states in (a). With that caveat the argument is correct.

The step D ⇒ rationality of characteristic polynomials on a single H^i is only referred back to the talk. Computing traces on H^i alone, rather than alternating traces over all degrees, needs care (e.g. Künneth-type arguments). The gap is not filled on this page.
Typos in the Cayley–Hamilton formula: it is typed as 'u^b − σ_1(w)u^{b-1}' but should be in w. 'whos that' should read 'shows that'.

ideas.what: The Lefschetz standard conjecture is equivalent to the existence of any algebraic isomorphism H^{2n-i} → H^i, given rationality of characteristic polynomials (e.g. under D). Hence it is independent of the polarization.
ideas.modern_name: Independence of the Lefschetz standard conjecture B(X)/A(X,L) from the ample class; criteria equivalent to B(X)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck / Kleiman (Kleiman, 'Algebraic cycles and the Weil conjectures', 1968; 'The standard conjectures', 1994)
ideas.where_published: Grothendieck, 'Standard conjectures on algebraic cycles' (Bombay 1968/69) discusses the variants of the Lefschetz conjecture. The detailed equivalences are worked out in Kleiman 1968.

ideas.what: Cayley–Hamilton trick: the inverse of an algebraic automorphism with rational characteristic polynomial is algebraic.
ideas.modern_name: Inverse of an invertible correspondence lies in the Q-algebra it generates
ideas.where_published: Kleiman 1968 (lemma used to show B(X) ⇒ Λ algebraic)

ideas.what: H^i is 'motive-theoretically' isomorphic to its dual H^{2n-i} (hard Lefschetz at the motivic level).
ideas.where_published: Grothendieck, 'Standard conjectures on algebraic cycles' (1969), implicitly

deep.surprise_reason: This is a clean, correct early (January 1966) formulation of equivalent forms of the Lefschetz standard conjecture and of its independence from the polarization. That content entered the literature essentially verbatim through Kleiman's 1968 exposition, for which Coates and Kleiman were the conduit. Its interest is historical: it dates and attributes the Cayley–Hamilton argument and the 'motivic self-duality' viewpoint. There is no new mathematics here.
transcription_corrections: In the Proposition line, 'C_1(X)' as typed is C_χ(X) (the χ is typed below the line).

Cayley–Hamilton formula: the typescript has 'u^b − σ_1(w)u^{b-1} + ... + (−1)^b σ_b(w) = 0'. The intended reading is w^b − σ_1(w)w^{b-1} + ... + (−1)^b σ_b(w) = 0, and the transcription's silent change to w is correct.
'v: H^i(X) → H^{2n-i}(X) the algebraic isomorphism': 'an' is struck and replaced by hand with 'the'.
'{+<n+}' handwritten insertions after 'every i' in both (a) and (b) are correctly read; the commas are struck.
